question:
Arrange the following UNESCO World Heritage Sites of India in chronological order of their inscription (earliest to latest):

1. Khajuraho Group of Monuments

2. Ajanta Caves

3. Sun Temple, Konark

4. Great Living Chola Temples
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 - 3 - 1 - 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct chronological sequence of inscription is Ajanta (1983) - Konark (1984) - Khajuraho (1986) - Great Living Chola Temples (1987). (यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल — अंकन का कालक्रम)

 

• Ajanta Caves (1983), Maharashtra: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist caves famous for their mural paintings depicting the life and previous births (Jataka tales) of the Buddha. India's very first World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1983, were Ajanta, Ellora, Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal.

 

• Sun Temple, Konark (1984), Odisha: Built in the thirteenth century by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, conceived as the chariot of the Sun God with 24 carved wheels drawn by seven horses. It is popularly called the Black Pagoda.

 

• Khajuraho Group of Monuments (1986), Madhya Pradesh: Built by the Chandela rulers between 950 and 1050 CE in the Nagara style; the Kandariya Mahadeva temple is the largest.

 

• Great Living Chola Temples (1987), Tamil Nadu: Comprise the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur (built by Rajaraja I), the temple at Gangaikondacholapuram and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other sites inscribed in 1986 include Fatehpur Sikri and the Group of Monuments at Hampi; 1987 additions include the Elephanta Caves and the Group of Monuments at Pattadakal.

 

• India's World Heritage Sites fall into cultural, natural and mixed categories. Kaziranga, Keoladeo, Manas and the Sundarbans are natural sites, and Khangchendzonga National Park is India's only mixed site.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 give incorrect sequences. The commonest error is to assume that Khajuraho, being older in date of construction, was inscribed earlier — but the question asks for the year of UNESCO inscription, not the year of construction.

question: Which of the following pairs of a temple architectural style and its distinguishing feature is correctly matched?
option_1: Nagara - the temple is enclosed by a boundary wall pierced by lofty gopuram gateways
option_2: Dravida - the temple stands within a compound wall, whose front gateway is called the gopuram
option_3: Vesara - a style found exclusively in the Kashmir valley
option_4: Nagara - the tower over the sanctum is known as the vimana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dravida - the temple stands within a compound wall, whose front gateway is called the gopuram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Dravida (South Indian) style, the temple is enclosed within a compound wall, and the front gateway in the centre of that wall is called the gopuram, which in later temples grew far taller than the main shrine itself. (द्रविड़ शैली — गोपुरम)

 

• Key contrasts between the two principal styles:

◦ Nagara (North Indian): the tower over the sanctum is the shikhara; there is generally no elaborate boundary wall or gateway; the temple is built on a raised platform (jagati); and there is usually no water tank within the complex.

◦ Dravida (South Indian): the tower over the sanctum is the vimana; there is a compound wall with gopurams; a temple tank is often present; and a large Nandi figure faces the Shiva shrine.

 

• Vesara is a hybrid of the Nagara and Dravida styles, found in the Deccan, particularly in Karnataka under the Chalukyas of Badami and the Hoysalas, and not in Kashmir.

 

• The three sub-types of the Nagara shikhara are the Latina (a simple square base curving inward to a point), the Phamsana (broader and shorter, with slabs rising in a straight incline to a single point), and the Valabhi (rectangular, with a vaulted, wagon-shaped roof).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The garbhagriha is the sanctum housing the main image, the mandapa the pillared hall, the antarala the vestibule connecting the two, and the amalaka and kalasha the crowning elements of a Nagara shikhara.

 

• Great Dravida examples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur, and the Meenakshi Temple, Madurai; famous Nagara examples include the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Khajuraho, and the Sun Temple, Konark.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The boundary wall with gopurams is a feature of the Dravida style, not Nagara.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Vesara style belongs to the Deccan; the distinct wooden-roofed temples of Kashmir form a separate regional tradition.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: In Nagara temples the tower is the shikhara; vimana is the Dravida term.

question: The Wangala festival, popularly known as the 'Hundred Drums' festival and celebrated in honour of the sun god Saljong, belongs to which tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Garo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wangala, the "Hundred Drums" festival, is the principal post-harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, also celebrated by Garos living in Assam, Nagaland and in Bangladesh. (वांगला — गारो जनजाति का उत्सव)

 

• It is celebrated in honour of Saljong, the Sun God of fertility, in thanksgiving for a good harvest, and marks the end of the harvest season and the onset of winter. It is generally held between October and November.

 

• The festival opens with the Rugala ritual, in which the village chief, the Nokma, offers rice beer, cooked rice and vegetables to Saljong. Its high point is the beating of hundreds of traditional drums (cheng) in unison, accompanied by dance in ceremonial dress and headgear.

 

• Meghalaya is home to three major tribes — the Garo, the Khasi and the Jaintia — and these communities are largely matrilineal, with descent and property passing through the mother.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of the North East:

◦ Nongkrem (Ka Pomblang Nongkrem) and Shad Suk Mynsiem — Khasi, Meghalaya

◦ Behdienkhlam — Jaintia, Meghalaya

◦ Hornbill Festival — Nagaland, the "Festival of Festivals"

◦ Chapchar Kut — Mizoram

◦ Bihu — Assam

◦ Losar — Arunachal Pradesh, Ladakh and Sikkim

 

• The Pongtu festival of the Tutsa tribe of Arunachal Pradesh is observed before the millet harvest to seek the blessings of the deity Rangkhothak.

 

NOTE

 

• The Khasi (Option 1): Celebrate the Nongkrem dance festival and Shad Suk Mynsiem, the dance of the joyful heart.

 

• The Jaintia (Option 2): Celebrate Behdienkhlam, observed to drive away plague and to seek a good harvest.

 

• The Mizo (Option 4): Celebrate the three Kuts — Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut and Pawl Kut.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

In Hindustani Classical Music, the Jhaptaal consists of ______ matras.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jhaptaal is a taal of 10 matras (beats), divided into four vibhags in the pattern 2 + 3 + 2 + 3. (झपताल — 10 मात्रा)

 

• Its clap pattern is marked X 2 0 3: the sam falls on beat 1, tali on beats 3 and 8, and the khali on beat 6.

 

• Its bols are: Dhi Na | Dhi Dhi Na | Ti Na | Dhi Dhi Na.

 

• The commonly asked Hindustani taals and their matras:

◦ Dadra — 6 matras (3+3)

◦ Rupak — 7 matras (3+2+2); it begins on a khali

◦ Keherwa — 8 matras (4+4)

◦ Jhaptaal — 10 matras (2+3+2+3)

◦ Ektaal and Chautaal — 12 matras

◦ Dhamar — 14 matras (5+2+3+4)

◦ Teentaal — 16 matras (4+4+4+4), with the khali on the 9th matra

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The basic vocabulary of Hindustani rhythm: taal is the rhythmic cycle, matra the beat, vibhag the section, sam the first and most emphatic beat, tali the clapped beat and khali the empty beat shown by a wave of the hand.

 

• The tabla is the principal percussion instrument of Hindustani music, and the pakhawaj accompanies the older dhrupad style; in Carnatic music the corresponding instrument is the mridangam.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1): The number of matras in Dadra.

 

• 12 (Option 3): The number of matras in Ektaal and Chautaal.

 

• 14 (Option 4): The number of matras in Dhamar, associated with Holi compositions.

question: Why is a badminton shuttlecock built with a conical skirt of feathers fixed to a rounded cork base?
option_1: The feathers make the shuttle heavier than a tennis ball so that it can be hit harder
option_2: The cork base allows the shuttle to bounce on the court like a ball
option_3: The rules require every shuttle to carry exactly twenty feathers for uniform weight
option_4: The design creates high aerodynamic drag, which steadies the flight and makes the shuttle always turn to travel cork first
solution_text:
The correct answer is The design creates high aerodynamic drag, which steadies the flight and makes the shuttle always turn to travel cork first.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A shuttlecock is an open conical arrangement of feathers fixed into a rounded cork base. This gives it very high aerodynamic drag and shifts the centre of mass to the heavy cork end. (शटलकॉक — वायुगतिकीय अभिकल्प)

 

• Because the mass is concentrated at the nose and the drag acts on the wide feathered skirt behind it, the shuttle is self-righting: no matter how it is struck, it turns in flight to travel cork first. This makes its flight path highly predictable, and gives badminton its characteristic steep, rapidly decelerating trajectory.

 

• A standard feathered shuttlecock has 16 feathers fixed in the cork base, weighs between 4.74 and 5.50 grams, and the feathers are 62 to 70 mm long. Feathers are traditionally taken from the left wing of a goose or duck, so that they all curve the same way and the shuttle spins consistently.

 

• A badminton court measures 13.4 m by 6.1 m (doubles width), the net is 1.55 m high at the posts, and a match is played on a best of three games of 21 points with rally scoring.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Badminton's world governing body is the Badminton World Federation (BWF), founded in 1934 and headquartered at Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The game takes its name from Badminton House in Gloucestershire, England.

 

• Major team championships are the Thomas Cup (men) and the Uber Cup (women); India won the Thomas Cup in 2022. P.V. Sindhu is the only Indian to have won two individual Olympic medals in badminton.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: A shuttlecock weighs only about 5 grams, far lighter than a tennis ball, which weighs around 58 grams.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: A shuttlecock is not intended to bounce; the rally ends when it touches the floor.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The BWF specification is 16 feathers, not twenty.

question: Who became the first Indian to win two medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games in the post-Independence era, achieving the feat in shooting at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manu Bhaker.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics — in the women's 10 m air pistol and in the 10 m air pistol mixed team event with Sarabjot Singh. (मनु भाकर — पेरिस 2024, दो कांस्य पदक)

 

• With this she became the first Indian since Independence to win two medals at a single Olympic Games, and the first Indian woman shooter to win an Olympic medal. Her first bronze also ended India's medal drought in shooting, which had lasted since the 2012 London Games.

 

• She hails from Jhajjar in Haryana and was awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

 

• India won a total of six medals at Paris 2024 — one silver and five bronze. The silver came from Neeraj Chopra in the javelin throw, and Aman Sehrawat won bronze in wrestling, becoming India's youngest individual Olympic medallist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before Independence, Norman Pritchard won two silver medals for India at the 1900 Paris Olympics in athletics, which is why Manu Bhaker's feat is described as the first in the post-Independence era.

 

• India's individual Olympic gold medallists are Abhinav Bindra (shooting, Beijing 2008) and Neeraj Chopra (javelin throw, Tokyo 2020).

 

• At the Paris 2024 Paralympics India recorded its best ever haul of 29 medals, including Harvinder Singh's gold in archery, the country's first Paralympic gold in that sport.

 

NOTE

 

• Sift Kaur Samra (Option 1): Won gold in the 50 m rifle 3 positions at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games with a world record, but has no Olympic medal.

 

• Esha Singh (Option 2): A pistol shooter who won multiple medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games.

 

• Rahi Sarnobat (Option 4): The first Indian woman shooter to win an Asian Games gold (25 m pistol, Jakarta 2018).

question: The New Development Bank, established by the BRICS nations, has its headquarters in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanghai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Development Bank (NDB), formerly called the BRICS Development Bank, is headquartered at Shanghai, China. (न्यू डेवलपमेंट बैंक — शंघाई)

 

• It was agreed upon at the 6th BRICS Summit at Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014 and began operations in 2015. Its purpose is to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies.

 

• Each founding member holds an equal shareholding, so no country has a veto. Its first President was K.V. Kamath of India. Its first regional office was opened in Johannesburg, South Africa.

 

• At the same Fortaleza Summit the BRICS nations also created the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA), a currency-swap framework of USD 100 billion to help members facing balance-of-payments pressure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• BRICS began as BRIC — a term coined by the economist Jim O'Neill in 2001 — with the first summit held at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. South Africa joined in 2010, making it BRICS.

 

• The grouping expanded from 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, with Indonesia joining subsequently. BRICS has no permanent secretariat; the chairmanship rotates annually.

 

• India has hosted BRICS summits at New Delhi (2012), Goa (2016) and virtually in 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Beijing (Option 2): Headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a different multilateral bank in which India is the second largest shareholder.

 

• New Delhi (Option 3): Headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA).

 

• Johannesburg (Option 4): Location of the NDB's first regional office, not its headquarters.

question: Which of the following best describes the book 'The Discovery of India'?
option_1: A travelogue of the Himalayan region written by Rahul Sankrityayan
option_2: A sweeping account of Indian history, philosophy and culture written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort
option_3: A biography of Mahatma Gandhi written by the American journalist Louis Fischer
option_4: A compilation of the folk tales of central India made by Verrier Elwin
solution_text:
The correct answer is A sweeping account of Indian history, philosophy and culture written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Discovery of India" was written by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1944, during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort for taking part in the Quit India Movement. It was first published in 1946. (भारत एक खोज — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

 

• The book traces the sweep of Indian history, philosophy and culture from the Indus Valley Civilisation to the freedom struggle, and is the source of Nehru's famous description of India as "an ancient palimpsest" on which layer upon layer of thought had been inscribed.

 

• It was adapted into the celebrated Doordarshan television series "Bharat Ek Khoj" (1988) by Shyam Benegal.

 

• Nehru's other well-known works are "An Autobiography" (also called Toward Freedom), "Glimpses of World History" — written as letters to his daughter Indira from prison — and "Letters from a Father to His Daughter".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some frequently asked book-author pairs:

◦ India Wins Freedom — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad

◦ The Indian Struggle — Subhas Chandra Bose

◦ Hind Swaraj and The Story of My Experiments with Truth — Mahatma Gandhi

◦ Gitanjali — Rabindranath Tagore

◦ Poverty and Un-British Rule in India — Dadabhai Naoroji

◦ Annihilation of Caste — B.R. Ambedkar

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Rahul Sankrityayan, called the father of Hindi travel literature, wrote "Volga se Ganga" and several travelogues, but not this book.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Louis Fischer wrote "The Life of Mahatma Gandhi" (1950), on which the film *Gandhi* was partly based.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Verrier Elwin was an anthropologist who wrote extensively on the tribes of central India and the North East, including "The Baiga" and "A Philosophy for NEFA".

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that determines the climate of a place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fertility of the soil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fertility of the soil does not determine the climate of a place. The relationship in fact runs the other way — climate, along with parent rock and vegetation, is one of the factors that determines the kind of soil that forms. (मिट्टी की उर्वरता — जलवायु का निर्धारक नहीं)

 

• The principal controls of climate are:

◦ Latitude — the angle of the sun's rays decreases from the equator to the poles, so temperature falls polewards

◦ Altitude — temperature falls with height at an average normal lapse rate of about 6.5°C per 1,000 metres

◦ Distance from the sea (continentality) — coastal places have a moderate, equable climate, inland places an extreme one

◦ Ocean currents — warm currents raise, and cold currents lower, the temperature of neighbouring coasts

◦ Relief and direction of prevailing winds — mountains block winds and create windward rainfall and leeward rain-shadow areas

◦ Pressure and wind systems

 

• Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place at a given moment, whereas climate is the average of weather conditions over a long period, usually taken as 30 years or more. The chief elements of weather are temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, humidity, cloudiness and precipitation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's climate is described as the tropical monsoon type, dominated by the south-west monsoon (June to September), which brings the bulk of the annual rainfall, and the north-east or retreating monsoon, which brings winter rain to the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu.

 

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD), founded in 1875 and headquartered at New Delhi, is the national agency for weather forecasting.

 

NOTE

 

• Latitude (Option 1), Altitude (Option 2) and Distance from the sea (Option 3) are all standard controls of climate, and therefore cannot be the answer to a question asking which factor does NOT determine climate.

question:
Which of the following about D. Gukesh is/are correct?

1.) In December 2024 he became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history.

2.) He won the title by defeating Ding Liren of China in a match held at Singapore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. Dommaraju Gukesh, born in Chennai in 2006, became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in December 2024, at the age of 18. (डी. गुकेश — सबसे युवा विश्व शतरंज चैंपियन)

 

• He won the title by defeating the defending champion Ding Liren of China in the World Chess Championship match held at Singapore, winning the decisive fourteenth game.

 

• He broke the record of Garry Kasparov, who had become world champion in 1985 at the age of 22.

 

• Gukesh had earned the right to challenge for the title by winning the Candidates Tournament at Toronto in April 2024, again as the youngest ever winner of that event.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Chess Champion; Gukesh is the second Indian to hold the world title.

 

• At the 45th Chess Olympiad at Budapest in 2024, India won gold in both the Open and the Women's sections for the first time.

 

• The world governing body of chess is FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), founded in 1924 and headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland. International Chess Day is observed on 20 July.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question: National Safety Day is observed in India every year on which date?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4 March.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Safety Day is observed on 4 March every year, marking the foundation day of the National Safety Council (NSC) of India, which was set up on 4 March 1966 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. (राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा दिवस — 4 मार्च)

 

• The observance was begun in 1972 and has since grown into a National Safety Week campaign, aimed at renewing the commitment of workers and management to safety, health and environment at the workplace.

 

• The National Safety Council is a non-profit, self-financing, tripartite apex body with its headquarters at Navi Mumbai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important national days:

◦ National Science Day — 28 February, marking the discovery of the Raman Effect by C.V. Raman in 1928

◦ National Youth Day — 12 January, birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda

◦ National Voters' Day — 25 January, foundation day of the Election Commission of India

◦ National Technology Day — 11 May, marking the Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 1998

◦ Engineers' Day — 15 September, birth anniversary of Sir M. Visvesvaraya

◦ National Sports Day — 29 August, birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand

◦ National Unity Day — 31 October, birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

 

NOTE

 

• 28 February (Option 2): National Science Day.

 

• 1 May (Option 3): International Labour Day, also observed as Maharashtra Day and Gujarat Day.

 

• 15 September (Option 4): Engineers' Day in India.

question:
Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): Most of the large rivers of peninsular India flow eastward and drain into the Bay of Bengal.

Reason (R): The Western Ghats form the water divide of the peninsula and are considerably higher than the Eastern Ghats, so the general slope of the Deccan Plateau is from west to east.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The major peninsular rivers — the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri — all rise in or near the Western Ghats and flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, where they form large deltas. (प्रायद्वीपीय नदियाँ — पूर्व की ओर प्रवाह)

 

• Reason (R) is true. The Western Ghats run close to the Arabian Sea coast, rise to an average height of about 900 to 1,600 metres, and act as the water divide of the peninsula. The Eastern Ghats are lower, averaging about 600 metres, and are discontinuous, being cut through by the rivers themselves.

 

• R correctly explains A. Because the Western Ghats are much higher and lie near the western edge, the general slope of the Deccan Plateau is from west to east — and rivers necessarily follow the slope of the land. The eastward flow is therefore a direct consequence of the relief described in R.

 

• The exceptions are the Narmada and the Tapi, which flow westward into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys and form estuaries rather than deltas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The highest peak of the Western Ghats is Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala, the highest in peninsular India; the highest of the Eastern Ghats is Jindhagada in the Arma Konda range. The two Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills.

 

• The Chotanagpur Plateau, an eastern extension of the peninsular block, is drained mainly by the Damodar, Subarnarekha, North Koel and South Koel, not by the Chambal and the Betwa, which are tributaries of the Yamuna flowing across the Malwa Plateau.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not an unrelated fact; the westward tilt of the highland is precisely why the rivers flow east.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: Chandrayaan-3, which achieved a soft landing near the lunar south pole in August 2023, carried which rover to the Moon's surface?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pragyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 by an LVM3 rocket from Sriharikota, and its lander Vikram made a soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, deploying the six-wheeled rover Pragyan (Sanskrit for "wisdom"). (चंद्रयान-3 — विक्रम लैंडर एवं प्रज्ञान रोवर)

 

• India thereby became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, after the USSR, the United States and China, and the first country in the world to land near the lunar south pole.

 

• The landing site has been named Shiv Shakti Point, and 23 August is now observed every year as National Space Day.

 

• The rover carried the APXS and LIBS instruments, which confirmed the presence of sulphur and other elements in the lunar soil; the lander carried ChaSTE, ILSA, RAMBHA-LP and a NASA laser retroreflector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandrayaan-1 (2008), launched by a PSLV, was India's first lunar mission and confirmed the presence of water molecules on the Moon. Chandrayaan-2 (2019) placed a successful orbiter, but its lander crash-landed.

 

• Aditya-L1, launched in September 2023, is India's first solar mission, placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1.

 

• The first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), India's planned space station, is targeted for launch around 2028, with the full station envisaged by 2035.

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram (Option 1): The name of the lander of Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3, after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, not the rover.

 

• Rohini (Option 2): A series of Indian satellites; RS-1 was the first Indian satellite placed in orbit by an Indian launch vehicle, the SLV-3, in 1980.

 

• Aryabhata (Option 3): India's first satellite, launched in 1975 with Soviet assistance.

question: Which statement best reflects the significance of mica in India's mineral economy?
option_1: Mica is burnt as a fuel in thermal power stations, and India imports most of its requirement
option_2: Mica is a metallic mineral smelted to obtain aluminium
option_3: India has rich reserves of mica, whose excellent insulating properties make it indispensable to the electrical and electronics industry
option_4: Mica has no industrial value and is used only as an ornamental stone
solution_text:
The correct answer is India has rich reserves of mica, whose excellent insulating properties make it indispensable to the electrical and electronics industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mica is a non-metallic mineral made of a series of plates or leaves that can be split into very thin sheets. It has excellent di-electric strength, a low power loss factor, insulating properties and resistance to high voltage, which make it indispensable to the electric and electronic industries. (अभ्रक — विद्युत उद्योग के लिए अनिवार्य)

 

• India has rich deposits of mica, chiefly in the Chota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand (Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt), in Bihar, in Andhra Pradesh (Nellore) and in Rajasthan (Ajmer to Bhilwara).

 

• Other important non-metallic minerals and their uses:

◦ Limestone — the basic raw material of the cement industry and a flux in iron smelting

◦ Gypsum — used in cement and in plaster of Paris

◦ Dolomite — used in the iron and steel industry

◦ Manganese, by contrast, is a ferrous metallic mineral used in steel making and dry batteries

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Minerals are broadly classified as metallic (further divided into ferrous such as iron ore and manganese, non-ferrous such as copper and bauxite, and precious such as gold and silver), non-metallic (mica, limestone, gypsum) and energy minerals (coal, petroleum, natural gas).

 

• Peninsular rocks contain most of India's coal reserves, metallic minerals, mica and other non-metallic minerals, whereas the sedimentary rocks of the western and eastern flanks hold most of the petroleum deposits.

 

• The Geological Survey of India (1851) and the Indian Bureau of Mines (1948) are the principal agencies dealing with mineral resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Mica is a non-combustible insulator, not a fuel, and India is well endowed with it.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Mica is non-metallic; aluminium is obtained from the ore bauxite.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Mica's importance is overwhelmingly industrial, not ornamental.

question: Once approved by both Houses of Parliament, a Proclamation of National Emergency continues in force for how long, unless revoked earlier?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Six months.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 352, once a Proclamation of National Emergency has been approved by both Houses of Parliament, it remains in force for six months from the date of the resolution, and may be extended indefinitely, six months at a time, with fresh parliamentary approval each time. (राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल — अनुच्छेद 352)

 

• The proclamation must be approved by both Houses within one month of its issue; if the Lok Sabha stands dissolved during that month, the period extends to thirty days from the first sitting of the reconstituted Lok Sabha, provided the Rajya Sabha has approved it meanwhile.

 

• Approval requires a special majority — a majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. This requirement was introduced by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

 

• The 44th Amendment also substituted "armed rebellion" for "internal disturbance" as a ground for Emergency, required the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet, and provided that the Lok Sabha may revoke the Emergency by a simple majority if one-tenth of its members give notice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Emergency has been proclaimed three times in India: in 1962 (Chinese aggression), 1971 (war with Pakistan) and 1975 (on the ground of internal disturbance).

 

• The Constitution provides for three kinds of emergency:

◦ National Emergency — Article 352

◦ President's Rule (State Emergency) — Article 356, approved by a simple majority, in force for six months at a time, up to a maximum of three years

◦ Financial Emergency — Article 360, which once approved continues indefinitely with no repeat parliamentary approval

 

• During a National Emergency, Article 19 is suspended if the Emergency is on the ground of war or external aggression, but Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended.

 

NOTE

 

• One month (Option 1): The period within which Parliament must approve the proclamation, not the period for which it remains in force after approval.

 

• Three months (Option 2) and One year (Option 4) are incorrect; the constitutional period is six months at a time.

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) is the launch vehicle ISRO normally uses to place remote-sensing satellites into sun-synchronous polar orbits.

Reason (R): PSLV was also the launch vehicle used for the Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) missions.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The PSLV is the vehicle ISRO routinely uses to place Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites into sun-synchronous polar orbits, which is exactly the purpose for which it was designed and from which it takes its name. (पीएसएलवी — ध्रुवीय सूर्य-तुल्यकालिक कक्षा)

 

• Reason (R) is true. Chandrayaan-1 (2008) was launched by PSLV-C11 and the Mars Orbiter Mission, Mangalyaan (2013), by PSLV-C25.

 

• However, R does not explain A. The fact that PSLV has also been used for two interplanetary missions is evidence of its versatility; it is not the reason why it is the standard vehicle for polar remote-sensing launches. That reason lies in its design, payload capacity and launch profile. R is therefore a true but separate fact.

 

• PSLV is a four-stage vehicle with alternating solid and liquid stages, has flown in several variants (PSLV-G, PSLV-CA without strap-on boosters, and PSLV-XL), and has earned the nickname "the workhorse of ISRO" for its long record of successful launches. In 2017, PSLV-C37 set a record by placing 104 satellites in orbit in a single flight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• ISRO's other operational vehicles are the GSLV Mk II, used for communication satellites in geosynchronous transfer orbit, the LVM3 (GSLV Mk III), the heaviest Indian launcher and the one human-rated for Gaganyaan, and the SSLV, designed for small satellites on demand.

 

• A sun-synchronous orbit is a near-polar orbit in which the satellite passes over a given point on the Earth at the same local solar time each day, which gives consistent lighting for imaging.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Although both statements are true, R states an additional achievement rather than the cause of A.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: Besides discontinuing the nomination of Anglo-Indian members, the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies for which groups?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, did two things at once. It extended the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies by a further ten years, and it discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to those bodies. (104वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2019)

 

• Reservation of seats for SCs and STs is provided by Article 334, which has been extended by successive amendments roughly every ten years since 1960.

 

• The nomination of up to two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha by the President, and of one to a State Legislative Assembly by the Governor, was provided by Articles 331 and 333. This provision lapsed on 25 January 2020.

 

• Note the important distinction: seats are reserved for SCs and STs, but Anglo-Indian members were nominated, because the community is too small and scattered to secure representation through election.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Anglo-Indian community is defined in Article 366(2) as a person whose father or any of whose male progenitors in the male line is or was of European descent, but who is domiciled in India.

 

• The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides for the reservation of one-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha, the State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly for women, to take effect after a census and delimitation exercise.

 

• Reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities for women — not less than one-third — was provided much earlier, by the 73rd and 74th Amendments of 1992.

 

NOTE

 

• Other Backward Classes (Option 1): There is no reservation of legislative seats for OBCs in the Lok Sabha or State Assemblies; their reservation applies to services and educational institutions.

 

• Economically Weaker Sections (Option 2): The 103rd Amendment, 2019, gave EWS a 10 per cent reservation in education and public employment, not in legislatures.

 

• Women (Option 4): Legislative reservation for women came with the 106th Amendment, 2023, and is not yet in operation.

question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023, electronic and digital records have been given which status?
option_1: They are admissible only as secondary evidence
option_2: They are treated as primary documentary evidence, at par with paper documents
option_3: They are treated as hearsay and are inadmissible
option_4: They are admissible only if corroborated by oral testimony
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are treated as primary documentary evidence, at par with paper documents.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023, which replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 with effect from 1 July 2024, expressly gives electronic and digital records the status of documents, so that they are admissible as primary evidence on the same footing as paper documents. (भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम, 2023 — डिजिटल साक्ष्य)

 

• The definition of "document" now covers e-mails, server logs, computer files, smartphone and laptop messages, website content, location evidence and digital voice mail.

 

• The Act also allows evidence to be given electronically, so that the testimony of witnesses, accused persons and experts may be recorded by audio-video electronic means, including from a designated location.

 

• A certificate in the prescribed form remains necessary to authenticate an electronic record produced in court, and the Act places emphasis on the chain of custody and the use of technology to establish authenticity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three new criminal laws, all in force from 1 July 2024:

◦ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860

◦ Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

◦ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872

 

• The BSA has 170 sections, against 167 in the old Evidence Act.

 

• Among the procedural changes brought by the BNSS are the videography of search and seizure, mandatory forensic investigation for offences punishable with seven years or more, and provision for Zero FIR and e-FIR.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Treating electronic records merely as secondary evidence was the earlier, more restrictive position; the BSA elevates them to primary evidence.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Digital records are neither hearsay nor dependent on oral corroboration; they require authentication through the prescribed certificate.

question: In Indian banking, the Business Correspondent (BC) model is primarily intended to serve which purpose?
option_1: To regulate the operations of foreign banks functioning in India
option_2: To provide insurance cover to the deposits held by bank customers
option_3: To fix the benchmark lending rates of commercial banks
option_4: To extend banking services to unbanked and remote areas through authorised agents acting for a bank
solution_text:
The correct answer is To extend banking services to unbanked and remote areas through authorised agents acting for a bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Business Correspondent (BC) model, introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in 2006, banks engage retail agents to deliver banking services at locations other than a bank branch. (बिज़नेस कॉरेस्पॉन्डेंट मॉडल — वित्तीय समावेशन)

 

• BCs act on behalf of the bank and may open accounts, accept small deposits and repayments, disburse small-value credit, and carry out transactions using hand-held devices and the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS). They are the backbone of the Bank Mitra network.

 

• Eligible entities include individuals, retired bank employees, kirana and medical shop owners, self-help groups, NGOs, cooperative societies, post offices and corporate entities.

 

• The purpose is financial inclusion — bringing banking within reach of villages that cannot support a full branch, and thereby supporting the Direct Benefit Transfer of government subsidies into bank accounts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), launched in September 2018 and wholly owned by the Government of India under the Department of Posts, delivers banking at the doorstep through the country's postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks, using the vast post office network.

 

• Payments banks may accept deposits up to a specified limit per customer and offer remittance and payment services, but cannot lend or issue credit cards.

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched in August 2014, is India's flagship financial-inclusion programme, offering a zero-balance account, a RuPay debit card and accident insurance cover.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The regulation of foreign banks is a function of the Reserve Bank of India, not of the BC model.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Deposit insurance is provided by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), which currently insures deposits up to Rs. 5 lakh per depositor per bank.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Benchmark lending rates are governed by the RBI's framework, currently the External Benchmark Lending Rate and the MCLR.

question:
Fill in the Blank:

The Bihu dance of Assam is performed chiefly to mark ______.
option_1: the end of the monsoon season
option_2: a funeral rite among the Bodo community
option_3: the Assamese New Year and the coming of spring
solution_text:
The correct answer is the Assamese New Year and the coming of spring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bihu dance is the folk dance of Assam, performed above all during Rongali or Bohag Bihu, which marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring, in mid-April. (बिहू — असमिया नववर्ष एवं वसंत का उत्सव)

 

• It is a joyous group dance performed by young men and women together, with brisk steps and rapid hand movements, to the accompaniment of the dhol (drum), pepa (a horn made from buffalo horn), gogona, taal and toka.

 

• Assam observes three Bihus in the year:

◦ Rongali (Bohag) Bihu — April, the New Year and spring festival, the most important and joyous

◦ Kongali (Kati) Bihu — October, an austere observance when granaries are empty and lamps are lit before the tulsi plant

◦ Bhogali (Magh) Bihu — January, the harvest feast, marked by community feasting and the burning of the Meji

 

• In 2023 a Bihu dance performance at Guwahati entered the Guinness World Records for the largest folk dance performance at a single venue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of the North East include Bagurumba (Bodo, Assam), Cheraw, the bamboo dance (Mizoram), Wangala (Garo, Meghalaya), Nongkrem (Khasi) and Hojagiri (Tripura).

 

• Some other state folk dances: Ghoomar and Kalbelia (Rajasthan, the Kalbelia dance imitating the movements of snakes), Garba (Gujarat), Bhangra and Giddha (Punjab), Lavani (Maharashtra), Chhau (Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal) and Nati (Himachal Pradesh).

 

• Sattriya, which also originates in Assam, from the Sattras or monasteries founded by Srimanta Sankardeva, is one of the eight classical dances of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Bihu is not tied to the retreat of the monsoon; the October Bihu is an austere observance, not a monsoon festival.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Bihu is a festive and celebratory dance, not a funeral rite.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The winter solstice is marked in India by harvest festivals such as Makar Sankranti, Pongal, Lohri and Magh Bihu, but the Bihu dance is associated above all with the spring Bihu.

question: The World Competitiveness Yearbook, which ranks economies on economic performance, government efficiency, business efficiency and infrastructure, is published by which institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The IMD Business School, Switzerland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Competitiveness Yearbook, and the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking derived from it, are published annually by the Institute for Management Development (IMD), a business school based at Lausanne, Switzerland. It has been issued since 1989. (आईएमडी विश्व प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता रैंकिंग)

 

• The ranking assesses each economy on four competitiveness factors, each carrying equal weight:

◦ Economic Performance

◦ Government Efficiency

◦ Business Efficiency

◦ Infrastructure

 

• Each factor is divided into five sub-factors, and the ranking draws on both hard statistical data and an executive opinion survey.

 

• Switzerland, Singapore, Denmark, Ireland and Hong Kong have consistently occupied the leading positions in recent editions, with Switzerland ranking first on the Infrastructure factor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indices are frequently confused in the examination; the principal ones are:

◦ Global Competitiveness Report — World Economic Forum

◦ World Competitiveness Yearbook — IMD, Switzerland

◦ Global Innovation Index — WIPO

◦ Human Development Index — UNDP

◦ World Development Report — World Bank

◦ World Economic Outlook — IMF

◦ Global Cities Index — Oxford Economics

◦ Corruption Perceptions Index — Transparency International

 

• The World Economic Forum, founded by Klaus Schwab in 1971, is also based in Switzerland, at Cologny near Geneva, and holds its annual meeting at Davos — which is why the two Swiss-based rankings are often mixed up.

 

NOTE

 

• The World Economic Forum (Option 1): Publishes the Global Competitiveness Report, the Global Gender Gap Report and the Global Risks Report.

 

• The World Bank (Option 3): Publishes the World Development Report and the Logistics Performance Index.

 

• The International Monetary Fund (Option 4): Publishes the World Economic Outlook and the Global Financial Stability Report.

question: According to the India State of Forest Report, which Indian state has the largest area under mangrove cover?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• West Bengal has the largest mangrove cover of any Indian state, on account of the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world, formed in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna. (पश्चिम बंगाल — सर्वाधिक मैंग्रोव क्षेत्र)

 

• Gujarat ranks second, chiefly in the Gulf of Kachchh and the Gulf of Khambhat, followed by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

• The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987), a Ramsar site (2019) and a Biosphere Reserve, and is the natural habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger. Sundarbans National Park also forms part of Project Tiger.

 

• Mangroves are salt-tolerant forests of the intertidal zone. They possess stilt roots for anchorage and pneumatophores (breathing roots) to obtain oxygen from waterlogged saline soil, and many species are viviparous, their seeds germinating while still attached to the parent tree.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mangroves act as a natural bio-shield, absorbing the energy of cyclones, storm surges and tsunamis, checking coastal erosion, serving as nurseries for fish and storing large quantities of "blue carbon".

 

• The MISHTI scheme — Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes — was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 for mangrove plantation along the coastline and on salt-pan lands, through convergence of MGNREGS, CAMPA and other funds.

 

• The India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published every two years by the Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Has the second largest mangrove cover in India.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Set up India's first dedicated Mangrove Cell, but its mangrove area is far smaller than that of West Bengal.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Has significant mangroves in the Godavari and Krishna deltas (Coringa), but again much less than West Bengal.

question:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The cotton textile industry is classified as a light industry.

Reason (R): It uses raw materials that are light in weight and turns out finished goods meant for direct use by consumers.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The cotton textile industry is classified as a light industry. (सूती वस्त्र उद्योग — हल्का उद्योग)

 

• Reason (R) is true. Cotton is a light, bulk-free raw material, and the industry's output — cloth and garments — goes directly to consumers.

 

• R correctly explains A. Industries are classified as heavy or light precisely on the basis of the bulk and weight of the raw materials used and of the finished goods produced. Since cotton is light and the finished cloth is light, the industry falls by definition into the light category. R therefore states the very criterion of the classification.

 

• By contrast, the iron and steel industry is a heavy industry because it uses bulky and heavy raw materials — iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite — and produces heavy finished goods; it is also a basic or key industry, since its output serves as raw material for other industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The main bases on which industries are classified:

◦ Raw materials — agro-based (cotton textiles, sugar, tea), mineral-based (iron and steel, cement), marine-based, forest-based

◦ Role — basic or key industries and consumer industries

◦ Capital investment — small scale and large scale

◦ Ownership — public, private, joint and cooperative sector

◦ Bulk and weight — heavy and light industries

 

• The cotton textile industry is India's largest organised industry in terms of employment, and is concentrated in Maharashtra (Mumbai, "Cottonopolis of India"), Gujarat (Ahmedabad, "Manchester of India") and Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore, "Manchester of South India").

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not an additional unrelated fact; the weight of the raw material and the nature of the product is the actual test used for the classification.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Green India Mission:

1. It is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

2. It aims to increase forest and tree cover and to improve the quality of existing forest cover.

3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The National Mission for a Green India (GIM) is one of the eight national missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), which was launched in 2008. (हरित भारत मिशन)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The Mission's twin objectives are to increase forest and tree cover on degraded and non-forest land, and to improve the quality of existing forest cover, so as to enhance ecosystem services such as carbon sequestration, biodiversity, hydrological services and the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. The Mission is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

 

• The eight missions under the NAPCC are:

◦ National Solar Mission

◦ National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency

◦ National Mission on Sustainable Habitat

◦ National Water Mission

◦ National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem

◦ National Mission for a Green India

◦ National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture

◦ National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Of these eight missions, the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture is the one implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, and the National Solar Mission by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy — a distinction often tested.

 

• India's forest and tree cover, as reported in the India State of Forest Report, stands at roughly 25 per cent of the geographical area; the National Forest Policy, 1988, set a target of 33 per cent.

 

• Under its Nationally Determined Contributions, India has committed to creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent through additional forest and tree cover by 2030.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each of them includes Statement 3, which wrongly names the implementing ministry.

question: Under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into which of the following?
option_1: Two separate States - Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh
option_2: A single Union Territory without a legislature
option_3: One State and one Union Territory
option_4: Two Union Territories - Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature, and Ladakh without a legislature
solution_text:
The correct answer is Two Union Territories - Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature, and Ladakh without a legislature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which came into effect on 31 October 2019, reorganised the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: (जम्मू और कश्मीर पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2019)

◦ the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, with a legislature, on the pattern of Puducherry

◦ the Union Territory of Ladakh, without a legislature, on the pattern of Chandigarh

 

• 31 October was chosen because it is the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, observed as National Unity Day.

 

• This followed the Presidential Order (C.O. 272) issued under Article 370(3) in August 2019, by which the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 ceased to operate, and Article 35A consequently fell away.

 

• With this reorganisation the number of States in India became 28 and the number of Union Territories 9; the later merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu in 2020 reduced the Union Territories to 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In In Re: Article 370 of the Constitution (December 2023) the Supreme Court upheld the abrogation, holding that Article 370 was a temporary provision, and directed that statehood be restored to Jammu and Kashmir and that Assembly elections be held. Elections to the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly were duly held in 2024.

 

• Article 370 appeared in Part XXI of the Constitution, headed "Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions".

 

• Under Article 3, Parliament may by law form a new State, alter the area, boundaries or name of a State, on the recommendation of the President and after the views of the State legislature have been ascertained — though those views are not binding.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Neither entity was made a State; both became Union Territories.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Two Union Territories were created, and Jammu and Kashmir was given a legislature.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: No State was created by the Act; the restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir remains a separate, subsequent process.
